# pingStation 3 JSON fixtures

Used by `test_pingstation`, `test_inputs`, `test_capture` and `test_status_poller`.

## Provenance

`traffic-1090.json`, `status.json` and `status-curly-quotes.json` are generated by `gen.sh`
with the project's own simulator `skycue-pingsim` (`gen.sh <skycue-pingsim> <fixtures-dir>`;
the exact generator command is recorded in the script). The values are synthetic: they come
from the first aircraft of `../readsb-sample.jsonl`, not from a device.

- `traffic-1090.json`: one aircraft datagram. The script fixes the timestamps (the simulator
  stamps the send time), adds `timeOfReceptionS` and `timeOfReceptionNS` (the latter as a
  string, as devices write it), a made-up 14-byte `rawData`, and pads the callsign with a
  trailing space.
- `status.json`: one `{"status":...}` datagram from the same run, with a fixed timestamp.
- `status-curly-quotes.json`: `status.json` with the quotes around the key `status` replaced by
  typographic curly quotes (U+201C/U+201D). That is not valid JSON, and the parser must reject
  it (no lenient parsing); the tests check that it is rejected and counted.

## Synthetic

- `uat-detail.json`: written by hand for the tests. A UAT target (`trafficSource` 1) with a
  geometric primary altitude of 5000 ft, a barometric secondary altitude of 5250 ft, on the
  ground, minimum-fuel emergency, emitter type 14 (B6), squawk 0007 and an 18-byte `rawData`
  whose content is made up (only its length matters).
